# Generated by `any gen chart` from this project's anywaye.yml.

# billing

The Helm chart billing is deployed from. The templates are the
contract; `values.yaml` is the deployment-time half — the file the
values commit edits.

## The loop

The chart is deployed by ArgoCD, pull-only, and the Application is
not this chart's: the substrate owns it — one static Application
per service, OCI-sourced, applied by install.sh (anywaye/notes/deployment.md,
"Who owns the Application"). A service repository commits none.
The only thing that can change the cluster is a commit: push a
values commit, Argo syncs, the box agrees with git. A hand edit
self-heals; rollback is `git revert`.

## Shipping the chart

The chart ships from the fleet's private OCI registry, because the
substrate is closed source and a pull-based system needs somewhere to
pull from:

    helm package chart
    helm push chart-0.1.1.tgz oci://ghcr.io/anywaye/charts/billing

The box pulls it with the read-only secret `values.yaml` names
(`imagePullSecrets`), created on the box once, out of band. The chart
names the secret and never contains a credential.

## Secrets

The service's environment arrives by reference: the Deployment reads
the secret `values.yaml` names (`secretName`) with `envFrom`. Create
it on the box:

    kubectl create secret generic billing-secrets --from-literal=...

Rotate a value by replacing the secret and restarting the pods — not
by editing a generated file.

### Two DSNs, and only one of them belongs in that secret

`DATABASE_URL` in `billing-secrets` is the APPLICATION's credential:
`billing_app`, the login role that owns nothing and is named in every
row-level-security policy. That is the role the pods serve as, and with the
policies FORCEd it cannot `ALTER TABLE … DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, cannot
`DROP POLICY` and cannot `DROP TABLE` — a compromised connection string is a
read-only one. `docker-compose.yml` carries the same split for a compose
stack, where it is one line of `DATABASE_URL` and a one-shot
`billing-migrate` container.

The OWNER's DSN (`billing`) is the migration and operator credential and
belongs nowhere in this secret. The pods no longer prepare their own schema
(`bin/docker-entrypoint` says why, and quotes identity's compose for the
rule), so a deploy runs the migration out of band, with the owner credential
in the operator's hand rather than in the Deployment:

    kubectl run billing-migrate --rm -it --restart=Never \
      --image=ghcr.io/anywaye/billing:0.1.1 \
      --env=RAILS_ENV=production --env=DATABASE_URL=<owner DSN> \
      -- ./bin/rails db:prepare

`db:prepare` and not `db:migrate`: on an empty database it creates the
schema, and it is also what installs the account boundary
(`lib/tasks/tenancy_substrate.rake` enhances it). It is idempotent, so
running it on every deploy is correct.

## Reaching the service

The chart installs no Ingress until a values commit says so:
`ingress.enabled` is `false`, and with it false `helm template` emits
no Ingress at all — a chart that suddenly routes traffic is a
defect. The services the fleet exposes (gateway, parlor) turn it
on in their values commit:

    ingress:
      enabled: true
      host: gateway.example.com

`className` is traefik, k3s's default (DEPLOYMENT.md:28). Set
`clusterIssuer` to a cert-manager ClusterIssuer — created once per
cluster by the substrate, not by the chart — and `tls: true` writes
the `spec.tls` block and cert-manager provisions the certificate.
Without an issuer there is no TLS: a secret nothing writes.

## Readiness

The probe is `/readyz`. That is the fleet's contract: every anywaye
service serves it, and the rollout waits on it. It is baked into the
template rather than left as a value, because a readiness path that
can be edited is a readiness path that can be pointed at `/up` — the
defect the kamal template had, which produced deploys that could
never go green.
